statement: Each transfer shifts one byte out on o_mosi and one byte in from i_miso.
Received bytes are returned on the response stream in order, one per transmitted command byte.
The master stops starting new transfers while the response stream is back-pressured.
Each command produces one 8-bit full-duplex transfer, MSB first.
i_cmd_last = 1 marks the last byte of a burst, and o_cs_n stays low for the whole burst.
SPI modes 0 to 3 are selected by i_cpol and i_cpha.
i_cpol and i_cpha are captured when a burst starts.
SCLK frequency is f(i_clk) / (2 x PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV).
There is no SCLK gap between back-to-back bytes.
SCLK pauses at its idle level and o_cs_n stays low.
No received byte is lost: one byte is shown on the response stream and at most one more is held inside the master.
Reset is asynchronous and active-low.
A transfer whose command is accepted at edge A covers 16·D i_clk cycles, starting at edges A through A + 16·D − 1.
The k-th transition of o_sclk (SCLK edge k) happens at edge A + k·D.
Odd SCLK edges (k = 1, 3, …, 15) leave the idle level of o_sclk. Even SCLK edges (k = 2, 4, …, 16) return o_sclk to the idle level.
The values of i_cpol and i_cpha captured at the first acceptance edge of the burst (CPOL_b, CPHA_b) apply for the current burst.
o_cs_n is 0 and o_sclk is at the idle level.
o_cs_n stays low for a trail of D cycles after SCLK edge 16 before going high.
SCLK frequency shall equal f(i_clk) / (2·D), where D is PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV i_clk cycles per SCLK half period.
Elaboration of m_spi_master shall fail with an error message.

o_mosi shall be 0.
o_rsp_valid shall be 0 and o_rsp_data shall be 8'h00.
o_cmd_ready shall be 1.
The master shall not accept a command.
The transfer in progress shall be aborted.
That byte shall be discarded without a response handshake.

The minimum o_cs_n high time of REQ-CS-005 shall not be required; after an aborted burst the high time is the reset duration plus time until next acceptance.
The master accepts a command at an edge only when i_rst_n = 1, i_cmd_valid = 1 and o_cmd_ready = 1 at that edge.
The master captures i_cmd_data as the byte to send and i_cmd_last as the end-of-burst flag of that transfer.
Values of i_cmd_data and i_cmd_last have no effect.
The master behaves as if the command had never been presented.
o_cmd_ready changes only at an i_clk edge or when i_rst_n is asserted, and does not depend combinationally on any input.
o_cmd_ready is 0 in every cycle in which o_rsp_valid = 1.
o_cmd_ready is 0 in every cycle starting at an edge from R to R + D − 2 (no such cycle when D = 1).
o_cmd_ready is 1.
o_cmd_ready is 0.
o_cmd_ready is 1 if the captured i_cmd_last is 0 and o_rsp_valid is 0, and 0 otherwise.
o_cmd_ready is 1 when o_rsp_valid = 0 and 0 when o_rsp_valid = 1.
o_cmd_ready is 0.
o_cs_n changes from 1 to 0 at edge A, starting a burst.
o_cs_n stays 0 until edge A + 17·D, where it changes to 1.
o_cs_n changes only at the edges given in REQ-CS-001 and REQ-CS-002 and at the assertion of i_rst_n.
The first SCLK edge of a burst comes exactly D cycles after o_cs_n falls (edge A + D).
o_cs_n stays 1 for at least D cycles.
The rise of o_cs_n does not depend on the response stream state (o_rsp_valid, i_rsp_ready, a held byte).
The master captures i_cpol as CPOL_b and i_cpha as CPHA_b.
CPOL_b and CPHA_b control o_sclk, o_mosi and the sampling of i_miso.
Changes of i_cpol or i_cpha have no effect on o_sclk, o_mosi, o_cs_n, i_miso sampling or response data.
Leading SCLK edges (odd k) are sampling edges and trailing edges (even k) are shift edges.
Leading SCLK edges (odd k) are shift edges and trailing edges (even k) are sampling edges.
o_sclk toggles at each of the 16 edges A + k·D, k = 1 to 16.
o_sclk does not change at any edge other than A + k·D, k = 1 to 16.
o_sclk equals CPOL_b (lead half period, Pause, Trail).
o_sclk equals NOT CPOL_b for odd k and CPOL_b for even k.
o_sclk equals i_cpol and follows changes of i_cpol combinationally.
o_sclk takes the value of i_cpol from edge R on.
The SCLK period over the joint is 2·D cycles with each half period D cycles.
Bits of each byte are sent MSB first: d[7], d[6], …, d[0].
o_mosi takes the value d[7] at the acceptance edge A.
o_mosi takes the value d[7 − j] at edge A + 2·j·D for j = 1 to 7.
o_mosi takes the value d[7 − j] at edge A + (2·j + 1)·D for j = 0 to 7.
o_mosi does not change at any edge other than those of REQ-MOSI-002 to REQ-MOSI-004, except at the assertion of i_rst_n.
o_mosi keeps the last value it was given, which is 0 after reset.
o_mosi is stable in the cycle before each sampling edge and does not change at any sampling edge.
o_mosi keeps d[0] unless the next command is accepted at that edge, in which case it takes the next d[7].
o_mosi keeps its previous value from the acceptance edge until SCLK edge 1.
The master captures i_miso as r[7 − j] at edge A + (2·j + 1)·D for j = 0 to 7.
The master captures i_miso as r[7 − j] at edge A + (2·j + 2)·D for j = 0 to 7.
The captured value is i_miso in the cycle ending at that edge, just before o_sclk makes the sampling transition.
i_miso has no effect.
The received byte r[7:0] of a transfer is made only of the 8 bits captured during that transfer.
Each accepted command produces exactly one response carrying the byte received during its transfer.
Responses are delivered in command acceptance order, across burst boundaries.
The master loads the received byte into o_rsp_data and sets o_rsp_valid to 1.
The received byte becomes the held byte.
The held byte is loaded into o_rsp_data and o_rsp_valid stays 1.
o_rsp_valid changes to 0.
o_rsp_valid stays 1 and o_rsp_data does not change.
o_rsp_data keeps the last byte loaded into it, or 8'h00 after reset.
o_rsp_valid and o_rsp_data change only at i_clk edges or at the assertion of i_rst_n.
i_rsp_ready has no effect.
The master never overwrites a shown or held byte before it has been taken and never delivers a byte twice.
At most two received bytes are pending at any time: one shown byte and at most one held byte.
A new transfer starts only when every earlier received byte has been taken, except the byte of the transfer ending at the same edge.
The new transfer uses that edge as its acceptance edge, with SCLK edge 1 D cycles after previous SCLK edge 16.
The master enters Pause.
o_cs_n stays 0, o_sclk stays at CPOL_b and o_mosi keeps its value.
Pause lasts until a command is accepted, without any time limit.
A transfer starts with acceptance edge A = P, in the same burst with the same CPOL_b and CPHA_b.
The master enters Trail and o_cs_n rises at edge A + 17·D.
The master does not start a transfer.
SCLK edge 1 (lead) must occur D i_clk cycles after command acceptance, where D = PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV.
o_cs_n must go low at the acceptance edge itself (0 cycles after command acceptance) for the first byte of a burst.
o_rsp_valid must become 1 16·D i_clk cycles after command acceptance.
o_cs_n must go high D i_clk cycles after SCLK edge 16 of the last byte (trail).
o_cs_n must stay high for at least D i_clk cycles between bursts.
Byte period inside a continuous burst must be 16·D i_clk cycles.
o_cs_n low time of an n-byte continuous burst must be 16·n·D + D i_clk cycles.
Minimum time between first acceptances of consecutive n-byte bursts must be 16·n·D + 2·D i_clk cycles.
The minimum period of single-byte bursts must be 18·D i_clk cycles.
The next command must be valid in the last cycle of the current transfer.
o_rsp_valid must be 0 in the last cycle of the current transfer, so the previous response must be taken within 16·D − 1 cycles of becoming valid.
The next transfer must not start at SCLK edge 16.
The burst must enter Pause, or Trail if it was the last byte.
That transfer's byte must become the held byte.
No new transfer may start until both bytes have been taken.
Responses must come out in command order.
The master shall keep using CPOL_b and CPHA_b until the end of the burst.
o_sclk shall change to i_cpol at the edge where o_cs_n rises.
The command shall wait without effect until a command handshake occurs.
The master shall not accept the command.
The master shall keep o_rsp_valid = 1 with the same byte.
The master shall not start any further transfer.
o_cs_n shall stay 0 indefinitely.
o_cs_n shall go to 1 and o_sclk to i_cpol at once, even in the middle of an SCLK half period.
The partial byte shall be discarded.
The master shall go to the reset state of REQ-RST-002 to REQ-RST-006.
Pending bytes shall be discarded.
The received byte of that transfer shall load into o_rsp_data at that edge, with o_rsp_valid staying 1.
The burst never ends; o_cs_n stays 0 and transfers continue as commands arrive.
The half-period count shall reach 255 without overflow, giving 255-cycle half periods and 4080 cycles per byte.
Verification must run every listed configuration, and since SPI mode is a run-time input, each configuration must be exercised in all four SPI modes.
With PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV=1, the smallest legal divider, SCLK must be f(i_clk)/2 and operate correctly in all four SPI modes.
With PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV=255, the largest legal divider, the half-period counter must work at full width and operate correctly in all four SPI modes with short bursts.
The environment shall release i_rst_n synchronously to i_clk.

statement: The command stream may change i_cmd_valid, i_cmd_data and i_cmd_last before acceptance; stability is not required.

Verification shall run all four modes in every configuration of section 11, with random bytes on i_cmd_data and from the slave model.
Verification shall use burst lengths 1, 2 and at least 16, mixing bursts with and without pauses (i_cmd_valid gaps of 0, 1 and many cycles).

The monitor shall also check lead, trail and gap times, the SCLK idle level and that o_mosi never changes at a sampling edge.
Verification shall check o_cmd_ready cycle by cycle against REQ-CMD-006 to REQ-CMD-012, including the blocked first D − 1 Idle cycles.
Back-pressure tests shall hold i_rsp_ready = 0 for long periods so that a held byte is created.
Back-pressure tests shall cover a response handshake exactly at edge A + 16·D (REQ-ERR-009) and random i_rsp_ready patterns.
Reset tests shall hold i_rsp_ready = 0 before reset where a shown or held byte is wanted, and assert i_rst_n between i_clk edges in each phase (Transfer, Pause, Trail, Idle gap, held byte).
Reset tests shall check that outputs take reset values at once and no response of the aborted transfer appears.

A test shall change i_cpol and i_cpha in the cycle just before a burst-start acceptance edge and check the new values are used.
An error test shall change i_cpol and i_cpha during a burst and check the burst finishes in the captured mode.

statement: The half-period counter shall be wide enough for D = 255, at least 8 bits.
The master shall use exactly D cycles for lead and exactly D cycles for trail.
The gap between transfers shall be at least D cycles, and exactly D cycles when the next command is already waiting.
A command shall be accepted only in Idle (after D − 1 blocked cycles), in Pause, or in the last cycle of a non-last transfer, and only if o_rsp_valid = 0.
o_cmd_ready shall have no combinational input path.
A transfer shall start only when o_rsp_valid = 0; no byte is lost, as one more byte can be held inside the master.
The response shall appear at SCLK edge 16 (A + 16·D) in all modes, also for CPHA = 0 where the last bit is sampled at edge 15.
o_mosi shall hold its last value, and be 0 after reset.
While o_cs_n = 1, o_sclk shall be combinational from i_cpol; while o_cs_n = 0 it shall be registered from the captured CPOL_b.
Mode input changes during a burst shall be ignored; captured values shall be used until o_cs_n rises.
Reset in the middle of a burst shall abort immediately and discard pending bytes; the gap guarantee does not apply across reset.
An illegal PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV shall cause an elaboration error.

not_verified.note: Same as REQ-PAR-001 elaboration error.

statement: o_rsp_data shall be 8'h00 after reset and otherwise keep the last loaded byte while not valid.
For D = 1 in Idle, o_cmd_ready shall equal NOT o_rsp_valid from the cycle o_cs_n rises.
There is no Pause timeout; o_cs_n shall stay low in Pause until the next command.
The master shall not enforce o_cs_n high for at least D cycles after reset release; the minimum gap is not guaranteed across reset.
